title: Provider configuration presence, thinking defaults and native FIM headers
pins: Per-field omitted/null/empty config precedence, reserved environment spellings, default thinking casting and request precedence, and quota headers surviving actual Mistral FIM dispatch. Drift can select a credential the caller meant to clear, enable a beta unintentionally, spend a different thinking budget or discard received quota. An empty value, an absent header and a zero quota must remain distinguishable to the consuming application.
scope: Only three shared providers. No live provider execution, timeout measurement, warning lifecycle, or broader provider coverage. Existing rate-limit offset and streaming trace divergences are unchanged.
construction: Native PHP manager and RequestPayloadMap; native TypeScript/Python constructors and injected provider transports. Synthetic environment values are isolated. Unexpected network is refused. FIM freezes UTC at 2027-01-15T08:00:00Z.
findings: Candidate observations are recorded per implementation. Agreement is derived only after all three have executed; it is not a correctness claim. Independent prewritten native predictions and port transport lifecycle tests are additional evidence.

discrimination.gap: Production mutation controls and their archived results are not yet delivered for this suite.
